class.name: FellowWater3D
class.brief_description: A body of water (lake, river, sea) with spectral wind waves, drawn to the horizon (FellowEngine).
class.description: The surface of a body of water at the node's height, to the horizon or within [member extent]. Wind waves are simulated on the GPU after Tessendorf: a JONSWAP spectrum (wind speed and fetch) with the Donelan-Banner spreading, evolved and transformed by FFT every frame in up to four cascades of different tile lengths ([member cascade_lengths]); the surface is displaced by them and shaded with their slopes. Where a [FellowShallowWater3D] covers the body ([member simulation_path]), its simulated surface is blended in: its height, its slopes and foam, and its flow carries the waves (flow mapping). Shading (one transparent material): reflections traced in screen space against the opaque scene, with the screen's view of distant scenery and the sky's IBL where nothing near is hit; Fresnel; refraction of the scene below through the screen texture; absorption along the light's path down and the view's path up ([member absorption]); in-scattering ([member scattering_color]) lit by the scene's lights, shadows included; foam from breaking waves (where the surface folds), shores ([member shore_foam_depth]) and the simulation; caustics on the refracted bottom computed from the waves' own slopes; the sun's highlight with a roughness that grows with the slope variance a pixel does not resolve, so a far surface shows a glitter path rather than a mirror image. The surface mesh is a polar grid around the camera; its displacement is band-limited to the grid's spacing. The node's rotation and scale are not used; [member extent] is axis-aligned. Needs the Forward+ or Mobile renderer; [code]rendering/fellow/fluid/enabled[/code] off stops the waves (the surface keeps its last state). Decision record [code]docs/decisions/0123-water.md[/code].

method.name: debug_get_displacement_image
method.description: The displacement of a cascade as computed on the GPU (x, y, z, foam; with mipmaps). Synchronous: for tests.

method.name: debug_get_spectrum_image
method.description: The initial spectrum of a cascade as uploaded (h0(k), conj(h0(-k))): for tests against a reference.

method.name: get_displacement_texture
method.description: The cascades' displacement (x, y, z in metres; foam in alpha), one layer per cascade, with mipmaps.

method.name: get_significant_wave_height
method.description: The significant wave height (four times the standard deviation of the surface) of the configured spectrum, in metres.

method.name: get_slope_texture
method.description: The cascades' slopes (sx, sz, sx², sz²), one layer per cascade, with mipmaps.

method.name: get_surface_mesh_instance
method.description: The internal mesh instance that draws the surface.

method.name: get_waves_gpu_time_ms
method.description: GPU time of the waves' compute passes in the last measured frame (RenderingDevice timestamps).

members.member: Absorption per metre for red, green and blue light. Pure water absorbs red (0.45); dissolved matter absorbs blue (the default is a temperate lake's greenish water).
Tile lengths of the wave cascades in metres, longest first; a zero ends the list. Each cascade holds the waves from six of its own fundamentals to where the next one starts.
The two depths at which the caustics are computed; the bottom interpolates between them.
Strength of the caustics on the refracted bottom (0 = off). They come from the cascades of at most 12 m.
Horizontal displacement of the waves (sharper crests, broader troughs). 0 = sine-like waves.
Shows one of the shading's terms instead of the water.
Size of the water's rectangle centred on the node (x and z, in metres). Zero: to the horizon.
Distance over which the wind has blown over water, in kilometres: a small lake's waves are short, the open sea's long.
Period of the flow mapping that carries the waves with the simulation's flow (two phases half a period apart).
Albedo of the foam.
Rate at which breaking waves' foam fades (1/s).
Foam produced where the surface folds, per unit of the Jacobian below [member whitecap_threshold], per sixtieth of a second.
Radius of the surface's grid around the camera, in metres.
Radius of the grid's innermost ring, in metres.
Segments of each ring of the grid (the rings grow by 1 + 2π / segments, so its cells stay square).
With [member wind_from_scene], how much the scene wind's gusts roughen the shortest waves (0: not at all).

Length of the screen-space reflection rays of the linear march, in metres (the hierarchical one, with the depth texture's mip levels, follows a ray across the whole screen). Where nothing is hit, what the screen shows in the ray's direction is reflected if it is farther than this.
Below this Fresnel factor (looking down into the water) no reflection ray is traced: the sky's IBL alone (faded in over 1.5 times it).

Most steps of a screen-space reflection ray. With the depth texture's nearest-depth mip levels ([code]rendering/fellow/postfx/depth_copy_nearest_mipmaps[/code], on) the ray crosses the screen hierarchically, a cell of a level per step, up to twice this many steps; without them about one step per 10 pixels of its length on the screen, at least 6, quadratically spaced from a per-pixel offset, then refined by bisection.
How far the waves shift the scene seen below, relative to the water's thickness and the distance (0 = no refraction).
The waves repeat exactly after this many seconds (the dispersion relation is quantized to it): precise phases however long the clock runs.
Roughness of the surface below the waves' finest scale; the waves the pixel does not resolve add to it.
Albedo of the light scattered back by the water's body (lit by the scene's lights).
Trace reflections against the opaque scene's depth. Off: only the sky's IBL is reflected.
Depth below which shores and objects in the water get foam, in metres.
Width of the band along the simulation's edges in which its surface blends into the body's, in metres.
A [FellowShallowWater3D] whose simulated surface this node draws where it covers the body (its own mesh is hidden). It must be axis-aligned.
Scale of the wind waves inside the simulation (they also fade in water shallower than 60 cm).
The [DirectionalLight3D] whose direction the caustics use. Empty: the scene's first visible directional light.
Advance the waves' clock with the process time. Off: set it yourself (deterministic playback).
Grid of each cascade (64, 128, 256 or 512 texels per side).
Scale of the waves' height and slopes.
Jacobian of the horizontal displacement below which breaking waves make foam (1 = flat; lower = fewer whitecaps).
Direction the wind blows towards, in degrees (0 = +X, 90 = +Z).

If [code]true[/code] and the scene has a [FellowWind3D], the waves follow its wind: [member wind_speed] and [member wind_direction] follow its speed and direction (the spectrum rebuilt when they change by 2 % or a degree), and its gusts roughen the shortest waves by [member gust_ripples] — darker, rougher water in a gust, a mirror in a lull.
Wind speed 10 m above the water, in m/s.
